title: Bind Japanese release assessment to immutable source identity
outOfScope: Declaring the final Japanese reassessment complete in this process corrective.
Changing Japanese product behavior, translations, installation steps, or general-fluency claims.
Starting documentation alignment, deprecated-assets cleanup, release publication, or plan cleanup.
Binding a checked-in report to its own Git commit through a circular self-referential digest.
Publishing or mutating any tag, GitHub Release, release asset, or release identity.

sources.reason: The current report uses a hard-coded prior Work Item identity and hashes evidence path names rather than the bytes of the implementation, tests, and documents being assessed.
Current drift tests mutate only the generated JSON or Markdown and do not prove that a semantically unchanged evidence-file edit makes the checked-in assessment stale.
check-release-preflight depends on check-japanese-capability, but the prerequisite does not receive or verify RELEASE_PREFLIGHT_SOURCE_COMMIT.
The release preflight binds release identity to an explicit source commit only after the Japanese prerequisite has run without that identity.
The current zero-blocker report contains no content identity for the assessed source/test/document evidence.
The mandatory order requires a workflow defect found during Japanese reassessment to be fixed before the reassessment resumes.

riskAssessment.reason: A report can remain green after assessed evidence bytes change, and a release preflight source assertion is not currently propagated to the Japanese prerequisite.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized continuous execution, required every discovered workflow defect to be fixed before resuming the affected Work Item, and requires Japanese capability to remain release-blocking.

preReviewWarnings: Content identity must avoid a circular digest over the generated report itself.
Generated transient Status bytes must not make the canonical Japanese report stale on every unrelated Work Item.
The corrective may report zero current capability blockers but must not claim that the final reassessment lifecycle is complete.
General Japanese model fluency and native-human translation quality remain explicit non-claims.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Bind implementation and final verification to the completed source-identity Contract.

acceptance: A1: The canonical assessment records a deterministic content identity over every stable repository source, test, corpus, and document file used as Japanese capability evidence, including the assessment implementation itself.

A2: The evidence identity lists normalized repository-relative paths and per-file SHA-256 values, rejects non-file or repository-escaping evidence, excludes generated transient Status output, and contributes to the top-level assessment digest.

A3: Changing even non-marker bytes in any bound evidence file makes the checked-in JSON and Markdown stale until the assessment is regenerated; changing unrelated repository bytes does not create false staleness.

A4: check-japanese-capability accepts an optional expected source commit, resolves it and HEAD to immutable commits, and fails with a Japanese-assessment-specific source mismatch before accepting the report when they differ.

A5: check-release-preflight propagates RELEASE_PREFLIGHT_SOURCE_COMMIT to check-japanese-capability, so the Japanese gate evaluates the exact checkout asserted for release rather than an unrelated HEAD.

A6: The regenerated machine JSON and derived Markdown identify the content-binding algorithm and assessed evidence digest, retain zero current in-scope blockers, and preserve the bounded repository-governance and general-fluency non-claim.

A7: Red-first regressions prove evidence-byte drift, missing/escaping evidence rejection, expected-source mismatch, exact-source success, and Make source propagation before implementation is accepted.
A8: The comprehensive plan, machine traceability, Contract, Summary, implementation, and acceptance evidence map bidirectionally and record this defect as a reusable process correction.

A9: Full quality, ai-finish archive, aggregate PR verification, exact-Head Hosted checks, merge, ai-close-work-item, local/remote branch deletion, and synchronized clean main complete before a fresh final Japanese reassessment starts.
A10: This Work Item changes no Japanese product capability, release metadata, public provider state, or later-stage completion status.
guidelines: Fix the reusable assessment and release-gate flow rather than manually relabeling the current report.
Use content identity for assessed evidence and runtime commit equality for the release checkout; do not invent a circular self-commit binding.
Treat missing, escaping, stale, or source-mismatched Japanese evidence as release-blocking.
Write and observe failing regressions before changing production behavior.
Keep general Japanese fluency and native-human translation quality as explicit non-claims.
Do not resume final reassessment until this corrective completes its full lifecycle.

intent.problem: The existing Japanese gate recomputes statuses from current path names and marker checks, but its case digests do not contain source/test/document bytes. The checked-in report also retains a hard-coded old Work Item ID. Therefore an evidence file can change without changing any marker and the gate still accepts the old zero-blocker report. During release, Make invokes this gate before the preflight recipe but does not pass RELEASE_PREFLIGHT_SOURCE_COMMIT, so the Japanese check cannot prove it ran on the asserted release checkout.
constraints: Do not solve the problem with a report digest that recursively includes the report's own commit or bytes.
Bind all stable evidence inputs while excluding generated transient Status output.
Do not broaden the claim beyond bounded repository-governance Japanese handling.
Do not alter Japanese product behavior or combine the final reassessment into this corrective.
Preserve direct make check-japanese-capability usage when no expected source commit is supplied.
Complete this independent corrective lifecycle before restarting the final reassessment.
intent.rationale: A deterministic evidence-file identity catches semantically invisible source drift without self-reference, while an expected-commit equality check proves the release gate runs in the exact checkout selected by release finalization. Together they prevent stale Japanese evidence from authorizing publication.

rawUserRequest: Continue the approved serial plan. Japanese capability is mandatory. If any problem is found during a Work Item, record it; if it is a workflow problem, fix the workflow first through its own complete PR, merge, archive, closure, branch-cleanup, and main-sync lifecycle, then resume the Work Item without another confirmation.

authorityEvidence.scope: Fix discovered reusable workflow defects and complete their full lifecycle before resuming the affected Japanese assessment.

declaredIntent.summary: Bind the Japanese capability report to the bytes it assesses and bind the release-time gate execution to the asserted release source commit.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A bound Japanese evidence file changes only whitespace or other bytes that do not alter existing marker predicates.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The evidence-source digest changes and the checked-in assessment is rejected as stale.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add a red-first regression that changes bytes while preserving the evaluated pass status and requires report_drift to reject the old report.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A source or test evidence path is missing, is not a regular file, or escapes the repository.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Evidence identity construction fails closed with the exact path in the diagnostic.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add red-first helper tests for missing, directory, absolute, and parent-traversal evidence paths.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The generated transient Cockpit Status changes for an unrelated active Work Item.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The canonical Japanese assessment remains stable because executable Status behavior is bound through implementation and tests, not transient generated output.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Assert the evidence-source path inventory excludes .ai/cockpit/current_status.md while retaining the Status generator, validator, Make target, and tests.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Release preflight asserts a source commit different from the checked-out HEAD.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The Japanese gate stops with a source-mismatch diagnostic before accepting zero blockers.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Create two real commits in a temporary Git repository and run the source-binding helper against mismatched expected and HEAD refs.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Release preflight asserts the exact checked-out HEAD commit.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The source binding passes and normal report freshness/blocker validation continues.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Use the same temporary Git fixture with equal expected and HEAD refs and assert the resolved immutable SHA.

scenarioCoverage.expected: The prerequisite Japanese command receives the exact variable through --source-commit before the release preflight recipe runs.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add a static Make regression for propagation and ordering, then verify a dry-run command line.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The source-binding corrective has not completed its PR/merge/closure/cleanup lifecycle.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Final Japanese reassessment, documentation alignment, cleanup, and release remain blocked.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Record exact PR Head, Hosted checks, merge commit, archive manifest, closure, and branch deletion before updating the serial stage.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user explicitly authorized completing the ordered remediation plan and fixing discovered reusable workflow defects before release.

rollbackNote: Revert the corrective PR; the prior zero-blocker report and this issue record remain historical evidence, and final reassessment stays blocked.
